findings.reason: The protected source implements the canonical wall-segment cache cleanly: it refreshes a row total and one total per column only at segment boundaries, evaluates only empty cells, and keeps the scan state explicit. It is concise, conventional, and already expert interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 361 and its Python maxKilledEnemies surface. The Reference preserves the three cell types, empty-cell placement rule, four-direction wall stopping semantics, required maximum, both source examples in order, and all four source constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064601226. Its defensive empty-grid return, row and column segment refreshes, cached totals, empty-cell maximum update, and return are identical to the protected app-local algorithm apart from the required LeetCode wrapper and annotations.

The legal wall-free benchmark tiers contain 64, 576, and 4096 cells, span 64x, and repeatedly exercise the segment totals at empty placements. The current source passes all 13 executions at -0.01 relative growth and 1.00x; a correct four-ray rescanner passes every benchmark output but fails only scaling at +0.48 and 16.37x.

The Approach accurately derives wall-delimited segment reuse, explains both refresh conditions and the no-double-count argument, traces the central source placement, and states O(mn) time with O(n) auxiliary space. Its alternatives and boundary notes match the protected implementation.

The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples in order, independent text equivalents of both source illustrations, blast blocking semantics, and all four constraints.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples now appear first and in source order with their exact matrices and outputs; the invented crossing and no-placement examples are correctly labelled trials.
The illegal empty-grid row was replaced by the legal 1x1 minimum, while visible single-row and single-column cases exercise both narrow rectangular orientations.
Walls split horizontal and vertical blast segments, crossing enemies combine both directions, and enemy-only, wall-only, and all-empty situations cover the absence of a productive placement.
All three legal cell values are exercised together with multiple walls, adjacent enemies, unequal segment strengths, and the rule that only a 0 cell may receive the bomb.

An independent four-direction ray oracle verified all ten authored results, all three benchmarks, and 21,243 exhaustive small grids; a checkerboard construction verified the 500x500 dimension boundary with expected result 500.
All ten correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 64-, 576-, and 4,096-cell workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
